Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
136 AM PST Sat Nov 28 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Mild temperatures will continue through Monday morning. 

* Strong, gusty winds are expected Sunday through Monday morning,
  with Sierra ridge gusts exceeding 95 mph and Sierra valley 
  gusts up to 50 mph.

* Widespread mountain snow and valley rain showers will arrive
  Sunday afternoon and continue through early Wednesday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...

We start off the forecast with a narrow ridge of high pressure
moving into the region, pushing out a weak trough that managed to
produce a few very light showers, if not virga, in northern 
Lassen and northern Churchill this evening. This ridge will lead 
to above-normal afternoon temperatures by 5-10 degrees today, 
with many valley locations reaching the mid to upper 50s. Sierra 
communities will see highs in the upper 40s to low 50s. Winds will
generally be light across the valleys today, though Sierra ridge 
gusts up to 40-50 mph will continue through this morning before 
gradually subsiding.

Sunday morning, the focus shifts to the approaching Pacific NW 
storm. Winds will begin to increase significantly across the 
entire forecast area. Sierra ridge gusts out of the southwest 
reaching 70-80 mph by Sunday morning. Sierra valley winds will 
increase throughout the morning as well, with peak gusts up to 50
mph. As the day progresses, gusty winds will extend into the 
Sierra Front. Sierra ridge gusts are forecast to exceed 95 mph, 
with NV valley gusts reaching 30-40 mph. Wind prone areas, 
especially in Mono County, may reach up to 50 mph. 

Precipitation will arrive in the Sierra midday Sunday, with light 
spillover into the eastern Sierra and Sierra Front. Latest NBM
PoPs for Sunday have a 90% chance of precip in the Sierra,
northern Washoe County, and northeast CA, 70-90% across Mono 
County, and 50-70% across the Sierra Front, dropping off to less
than 10% over Churchill and Mineral counties. Initially, snow 
levels will be high, around 8000-8500 feet, falling to around 
7000-7500 feet for the Tahoe Basin and southern Sierra, and 
potentially as low as 6500 feet for northeastern California by 
early Monday morning. The heaviest precip will subside by Monday
morning, with lingering showers in the Sierra Monday afternoon. 
Total snow amounts with this system through Monday night will be 
fairly light (2-6" along the Sierra crest, with up to 9" on the 
highest peaks).

Starting Tuesday, the forecast is still coming into focus. The 
long range models are still trying to get a handle on another 
system Tuesday, which ultimately lowers our confidence. The upper
level pattern looks to have a trough off the West Coast split as 
it moves over the western US, creating some uncertainty in the 
track of the storm. Over the last few models runs, the storm has
been taking a more southerly track, leaving the Sierra on the 
northern edge of the storm. Snow amounts have also been trending 
down over the past couple days, so we'll see in the upcoming days
if that levels out or continues to go down. Then later on next 
week from Wednesday through Friday, we will likely see another 
break in the storms, with more storms on the horizon next weekend.

-Justin

&&

.AVIATION...

KRNO Forecast: 

* VFR conditions with light winds and BKN-OVC mid-high level
  clouds today. A temperature inversion may produce minor
  slantwise visibility reductions around KRNO this morning 
  through 18Z. Increasing southwest FL100 winds (up to 40 kt) 
  bring increased turbulence and periods of LLWS late Saturday 
  evening into Sunday morning.

Regional Outlook: 

* VFR for all main terminals, except patchy FZFG with LIFR
  conditions for KTRK through 15-16Z this morning. Valley
  inversions may produce minor slantwise visibility reductions
  this morning for KCXP/KMEV. Otherwise, southwest winds will 
  start to increase late tonight into Sunday morning, bringing 
  increased turbulence and periods of LLWS.
  
24-72 Hour Outlook: 

* VFR conditions with clearing skies early Sunday morning. FL100
  winds increase out of the southwest Sunday morning ahead of our
  next storm system, leading to additional mountain wave
  turbulence and LLWS. Surface winds and chances for rain showers
  increase at all sites Sunday afternoon, and even a 15% chance
  for lightning in the Sierra. MVFR/brief IFR for KTRK-KTVL, while
  other sites have a lower 30-50% chance of lighter rain showers
  Sunday evening and overnight. Showers will mostly wrap up early
  Monday morning, though Sierra terminals may see some lingering
  showers Monday afternoon.
  
-Justin
